text:
**Short version:** Qi2 and Qi2.2 are open standards from the Wireless Power Consortium (WPC). MagSafe is Apple's own branding and certification, and its current charger meets the newest Qi2 standard.

| | Qi2 | Qi2.2 (Qi2 25W) | MagSafe |
|---|---|---|---|
| Who defines it | WPC | WPC | Apple |
| Max power | 15W | 25W | 15W for most iPhones, up to 25W for newer ones |
| Magnets | Yes | Yes | Yes |

**Qi2** added a magnetic ring to Qi, with Apple contributing its MagSafe tech to the standard. The magnets align the phone and charger, which improves efficiency and speed. It is capped at 15W ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey)).

**Qi2.2** (the WPC brands it "Qi2 25W") raises the cap to 25W. The WPC says that's nearly 70% more power and about 0 to 50% in 30 minutes ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)). The first certified products appeared in July 2025.

**MagSafe** is Apple's version. Per [Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html):
- Apple-certified accessories deliver 15W to most iPhones and up to 25W to iPhone 16 and later, with Apple's latest charger or a Qi2 25W-certified one.
- Certified chargers also add an NFC identification chip and a magnetometer to prevent compass interference.
- Uncertified "MagSafe-compatible" chargers are usually just 7.5W with magnets to hold the phone.

Apple's current MagSafe Charger is itself certified for Qi2 25W and Qi ([Apple](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m)).

**Your phone sets the real speed** ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047), [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)):
- iPhone 17 and 17 Pro, and the 18 Pro models: up to 25W
- iPhone 16 and 16 Pro: 22.5W
- iPhone Air: 20W
- iPhone 17e and iPhone 15 and earlier: 15W
- Pixel 10 Pro XL: Qi2.2 at 25W. Other Pixel 10 models: Qi2 at 15W.
- Samsung Galaxy S26 series: "Qi2 Ready," so it needs a magnetic case for 15W.

**What to buy:** For an iPhone 16 or newer, look for "Qi2.2" or "Qi2 25W" on the box. For an older iPhone, a 15W Qi2 or MagSafe charger is enough. Apple's [MagSafe Charger](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m) is the simple choice. You'll also need a 30W or higher USB-C adapter for the full 25W.
